findings.title: PMKID disclosed in EAPOL message 1
findings.detail: AP 04:42:1a:19:88:f8 ("testnetworkRPT88") included a PMKID in message 1. Because the PMKID is HMAC-SHA1(PMK, "PMK Name" || AP || STA), this one frame supports an offline dictionary attack on the passphrase with no client and no full handshake required
evidence: remediation: WPA3-SAE, or disable PMKID caching on the AP

findings.title: Complete four-way handshake captured
findings.detail: the full handshake between a8:42:a1:0e:7f:b2 and 04:42:1a:19:88:f8 ("testnetworkRPT88") is in this capture. WPA2 derives the PTK from the PMK and the two nonces with no key exchange, so recovering the passphrase later decrypts this session retroactively -- WPA2-PSK has no forward secrecy
evidence: remediation: WPA3-SAE runs a Dragonfly key exchange per session, so a later passphrase compromise reveals nothing

findings.title: Unprotected deauth on an MFP-required network
findings.detail: "testnetworkRPT88" (04:42:1a:19:88:f8) requires management frame protection, so compliant clients will ignore these unprotected frames -- the attack is visible but ineffective

findings.title: Low-confidence observations excluded from the findings
findings.detail: a real access point beacons about ten times a second, so a BSSID seen once in a capture of any length is far more likely to be a corrupted frame than a network; these are listed here rather than reported as findings
evidence: 37 frames had a structurally invalid transmitter address (group bit set) and were excluded from network discovery entirely
findings.benign_explanation: a genuine but very distant access point, or one captured for only a moment while channel hopping, can also appear this way
